title: THE CONFESSION THAT DID NOT LAST

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses left Pharaoh and went out of the city. He spread out his hands towards the Lord; the thunder and hail stopped, and the rain no longer poured down on the land. When Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped, he sinned again: He and his officials hardened their hearts. So Pharaoh's heart was hard and he would not let the Israelites go, just as the Lord had said through Moses." - Exodus 9:33-35 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The storm stops. The confession evaporates. He sinned again.

Just verses earlier Pharaoh had said, I have sinned, the Lord is in the right. Now, with clear skies overhead, he hardens his heart along with his officials.

Notice the trigger once more: when Pharaoh saw that the rain and hail and thunder had stopped. It was relief that undid him, not pressure. This is now the settled pattern of the man's life.

Take this as a mirror rather than merely a history lesson. Most of us have prayed something in a hospital corridor or a sleepless night that we quietly forgot once the crisis passed.

The remedy is not to wish for more storms. It is to build habits that hold in fair weather — regular time in Scripture, honest fellowship, faithful worship when nothing is wrong. Jesus said that the one who hears His words and puts them into practice is like a man whose house stood because its foundation was on rock (Lk 6:47-49).

Foundations are laid before the storm, and they are what remain after it.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What did I promise God in my last crisis, and have I kept it?
2. What habit could I build now, in calm weather, that would hold me later?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep me faithful when the pressure lifts. Build in me habits that will hold in every season. Amen.
